Anaguta Ancestral Trail: Our Expedition to the Sacred Peaks and Amanza Waterfalls

By Anaguta Tradomodern Media

The story of a people is not only found in books. It is found in the mountains they climbed, the waterfalls they revered, and the stories elders still carry.

On Saturday, October 24, 2026 the Anaguta Tradomodern team carried out a heritage documentation expedition across two of the most significant sites of Anaguta land in Jos North, Plateau State.

The Journey

What started as a routine morning meetup quickly became a rigorous trek through bush paths, rocky outcrops, and steep ancestral routes. The team, which included both male and female members, navigated difficult terrain that once served as home and fortress for Anaguta ancestors.

The peak offered more than a view. It offered perspective. From the top, the entire landscape of Anaguta land unfolds — a reminder of why our ancestors chose the high ground for safety, identity, and spirituality.

The History Session

A major highlight of the expedition was an oral history session with an Anaguta Elder who narrated the authentic origin and significance of the mountain. This is history you will not find on Google. The full video interview will be published on our platforms in the coming days.

Amanza Waterfalls

The team proceeded to Amanza Waterfalls, a sacred and historical landmark central to Anaguta identity. Known for its cultural and historical depth, Amanza remains one of the most important heritage sites in Jos.

Why This Project Matters

At Anaguta Tradomodern, our mission is simple: Document. Preserve. Project.

Expeditions like this are part of our ongoing effort to physically trace, record, and share Anaguta heritage before it is lost to urbanization and misrepresentation. We are grateful to all team members who participated.

Team: Emmanuel Kinaru, Garba Joseph, Mayam Dauji, Zamuta Ishaya, Kefas Ishaya, Enoch Barandu, Nanman Danan
Documentation by: Anaguta Tradomodern Media
Location: Anaguta Mountains & Amanza Falls, Jos, Plateau State
